metadata.scope: The two independent encryption-at-rest controls that protect a k0s control-plane node built by this pipeline: vTPM-backed LUKS disk encryption of COS_PERSISTENT (Kairos kcrypt) and vTPM-backed etcd Secrets envelope encryption (sceau, a KMSv2 plugin). Companion model to docs/design/vtpm-kairos-k0s-encryption.md, which also carries the validated command-line proof for every relationship below. Cross-repository detail (banlieue's scheduler internals, sceau's own repo) is summarized here as a single node; the owning repository is the source of truth for it.

nodes.name: Vault vCenter Credential
nodes.description: The vCenter service-account username/password held in Vault -- the actual root of trust for this entire document (§2a). Two independent paths consume it: the image pipeline's govc-driven template build (one-time, out of band, no banlieue involvement) and banlieue-provider-vsphere's Provider.spec.connection.credentialsRef Secret (every clone_vm + add_tpm_device call). VMClass.spec.tpm_enabled and the scheduler's failure-domain gate are authorization policy layered on top of this credential, not a substitute for securing it -- anyone holding it can attach a VirtualTPM directly via govc, bypassing banlieue entirely.

nodes.name: ESXi Host Physical TPM Attestation
nodes.description: The crypto team's enrollment of each ESXi host's physical TPM 2.0 chip: Intel TXT measured boot, remote attestation against expected PCR values, and host state-encryption sealed to that physical TPM (protectionMode=tpm, requireSecureBoot=true) -- vSphere's TPM-based key persistence for KMS-derived keys the host has already fetched (§3c). Confirmed live via govc host.tpm.info/host.tpm.report across all hosts in the environment. A distinct trust root from the Vault vCenter credential and from vCenter's KMIP Key Provider registration -- owned by a different team, verified independently.

nodes.name: Kairos Node Image
nodes.description: The Kairos image (from the CI image pipeline in the companion doc's §1) a k0s controller/worker boots from, carrying the cloud-config that declares install.encrypted_partitions (§4) and, once §7's open item lands, sceau's binary and disabled-by-default systemd unit.

nodes.name: banlieue Scheduler
nodes.description: banlieue-controller's scheduler, which only places a VMClass.spec.tpm_enabled=true workload onto a Provider whose failure domain advertises the 'vtpm' feature (ADR-0039). Owned by the banlieue repository; summarized here as one node.

nodes.name: banlieue-provider-vsphere
nodes.description: Sequences clone (powered off) -> add_tpm_device (ReconfigVM_Task with a VirtualTPM device spec) -> power on. Owned by the banlieue repository.

nodes.name: vCenter KMIP Key Provider
nodes.description: vCenter's registered Key Provider 'NonProd KMIP', backed by a Thales CipherTrust/KeySecure server at kms.example.com:5696. Gates whether vSphere permits a VirtualTPM device to be created at all; verified live via 'govc kms.ls' (status=green, useAsDefault=true) in §3a. Plays no further role once a VM's vTPM exists.

nodes.name: Example Corp Internal CA
nodes.description: The internal CA that issues both sides of the KMIP mutual-TLS trust: the KMIP server certificate (CN=kmip-server.example.com) and vCenter's client certificate (CN=vcenter-client-01). Confirmed live via 'govc kms.ls -json' in §3a, not assumed from config.

nodes.name: vTPM Device
nodes.description: The per-VM virtual TPM 2.0 device attached by banlieue-provider-vsphere before first boot. Confirmed as virtual (not host-level) via the ACPI vendor string 'VMWARE VMW_TPM2' in the node's boot log (§4a). Root of trust for both kcrypt (disk) and sceau (etcd Secrets) — distinct TPM object hierarchies, same hardware.

nodes.name: Kairos kcrypt
nodes.description: Kairos's early-boot disk-encryption component (kairos-immucore). Uses the 'Local TPM NV passphrase' method: seals a passphrase into a TPM NV index (not a LUKS2 metadata token) and unlocks COS_PERSISTENT on every boot with zero human interaction and zero network calls. Confirmed live via boot-log grep in §4a.

nodes.name: COS_PERSISTENT (LUKS2 volume)
nodes.description: The encrypted ext4-on-LUKS2 volume bind-mounted onto every sensitive k0s/etcd path: /var/lib/etcd, /var/lib/k0s, /etc/k0s, /opt/k0s. Confirmed via 'lsblk -f' in §4a.

nodes.name: k0s Controller (kube-apiserver, etcd)
nodes.description: The k0s controller process tree running on the node: kube-apiserver (wired with --encryption-provider-config), etcd (the storage backend), and the other control-plane components. Runs kube-apiserver as uid=kube-apiserver, gid=0/root — a permissions detail that matters for sceau's socket ACL (§5a).

nodes.name: sceau
nodes.description: Rust KMSv2 plugin (firestoned/sceau, image at registry.example.com/sceau) serving kube-apiserver over a root-owned unix socket at /run/sceau/sceau.sock. On every start, re-derives the same deterministic RSA-2048 SRK from the vTPM device (TPM2_CreatePrimary) and seals each Secret's DEK as a keyed-hash object under it -- no persisted key-encryption key anywhere. key_id is derived from the SRK's Name, so it is stable per-TPM across restarts (validated in §5a) and rejected if it ever doesn't match.

nodes.name: etcd Secrets (KMSv2 envelope)
nodes.description: Kubernetes Secret objects as stored in etcd's key space (/registry/secrets/...). Verified via a raw 'etcdctl get' bypassing the Kubernetes API in §5a: the value carries the k8s:enc:kms:v2:sceau: prefix and binary ciphertext embedding sceau's key_id -- no Secret plaintext appears in the raw record.

relationships.description: One-time, out of band, before banlieue is involved: the image pipeline's build scripts export GOVC_USERNAME/GOVC_PASSWORD from Vault/CI secrets and call govc directly to create the base Kairos VM template banlieue later clones.

banlieue-provider-vsphere reads this same class of credential from a Kubernetes Secret (Provider.spec.connection.credentialsRef) for every clone_vm and add_tpm_device ReconfigVM_Task call. In this deployment the Secret is materialized manually from Vault, not kept in sync by an automated External Secrets pull (§7 open item).

Host TPM attestation status (accepted/rejected) is a precondition vSphere associates with trusting a given ESXi host for encrypted-VM operations -- whether it is a hard block or advisory-only in this vSphere version/Trust Authority configuration is an open item (§7), not yet independently confirmed.
The Kairos node image, once cloned and booted, becomes the running k0s controller node these encryption controls apply to.
A VMClass.spec.tpm_enabled=true workload is only scheduled onto a Provider advertising the 'vtpm' feature; the scheduler hands off to banlieue-provider-vsphere to actually attach the device.

clone (powered off) -> add_tpm_device (ReconfigVM_Task + VirtualTPM) -> power on. The hard requirement is attaching before first boot, since kcrypt seals against the TPM during the unattended install.
vCenter only permits a VirtualTPM device to be created while its registered Key Provider is healthy. Verified live: govc kms.ls reported status=green. This is the KMS's only role in the whole chain.

Both sides of the KMIP mutual-TLS handshake -- the KMIP server's certificate and vCenter's client certificate -- chain to this internal CA. Confirmed via govc kms.ls -json (§3a): clientTrustServer=true and serverTrustClient=true.

kcrypt seals its LUKS unlock passphrase into a TPM NV index on this vTPM at first boot, and unseals it (no human, no remote server) on every subsequent boot. Confirmed via boot-log grep: 'Using local TPM NV passphrase for encryption' (§4a).
cryptsetup luksFormat / luksOpen against COS_PERSISTENT using the TPM-unsealed passphrase, before /var/lib/etcd and the rest of k0s's state can be mounted.

/var/lib/etcd, /var/lib/k0s, /etc/k0s and /opt/k0s are bind-mounted onto the encrypted volume, so all control-plane state at rest is disk-encrypted independently of whatever sceau does at the Secret-object level.

kube-apiserver's KMSv2 provider (--encryption-provider-config) dials sceau's unix socket on every Secret read/write. Requires the socket to be group=root (gid=0), matching how k0s runs kube-apiserver -- a gotcha found during validation (§5a).

On every start, sceau recreates the same deterministic SRK from the vTPM (TPM2_CreatePrimary) and uses it to seal/unseal each Secret's DEK -- no key material persists outside the TPM. Confirmed by restarting sceau and observing the identical key_id re-derived (§5a).
Once sceau wraps a Secret's DEK, kube-apiserver writes the envelope-encrypted value to etcd. Confirmed via a raw etcdctl read showing the k8s:enc:kms:v2:sceau: prefix and no Secret plaintext (§5a).
